```{r, include = F}
library(tidyverse)
library(ggpubr)
library(kableExtra)

plot_theme <- readRDS("scripts/plot_theme.RDS")

```


```{r, include = F}
hat_by_pbt_chk <- readRDS("output/hat_by_pbt_fromR.RDS")

hat_by_pbt_spreadsheet <- read.csv("data_inputs/2025/hat_by_pbt_check.csv")
hat_by_pbt_spreadsheet <- hat_by_pbt_spreadsheet %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = c("F", "M", "jack"), names_to = "Sex", values_to = "spreadsheet_count")

check_output_hatbypbt <- full_join(hat_by_pbt_chk, hat_by_pbt_spreadsheet, 
                                   by = c("Sex", "brood_year", "RelSite"))  

hat_by_pbt_plot <- ggplot(check_output_hatbypbt, aes(x = spreadsheet_count, y = total)) + 
  geom_abline(slope = 1, linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(size = 4, shape = 21, color = "black", fill = "grey50") + 
  plot_theme + 
  xlab("Excel method") + 
  ylab("R method") + 
  scale_x_continuous(expand = c(0, 0), limits = c(0, 2000)) + 
  scale_y_continuous(expand = c(0, 0), limits = c(0, 2000)) + 
  ggtitle("")
  
```


```{r, include = F}
final_estimates <- readRDS("output/final_estimates.RDS")

final_totals <- read.csv("data_inputs/2025/final_totals_check.csv")
final_totals <- final_totals %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = c("F", "M", "jack"), names_to = "Sex", values_to = "spreadsheet_count")


check_final <- full_join(final_estimates, final_totals, by = c("Sex", "RelSite", "brood_year", "age", "rearing" , "origin"))

check_final <- check_final %>%
  mutate(total = if_else(is.na(total), 0, total)) %>%
  mutate(spreadsheet_count = if_else(is.na(spreadsheet_count), 0, spreadsheet_count)) %>%
  mutate(diff = total - spreadsheet_count) %>%
  mutate(pct_diff = (diff/spreadsheet_count)*100)%>%
  filter(!(total == 0 & spreadsheet_count == 0))

summary(check_final$diff)
check_final %>% filter(is.na(diff))




raw_diff_hist <- ggplot(check_final, aes(x = diff)) + 
  geom_histogram(fill = "grey", color = "black", binwidth = 5)  + 
  plot_theme + 
  xlab("Difference between estimates") + 
  ylab("Count") + 
  scale_x_continuous(expand = c(0, 0), limits = c(-50, 150)) + 
  scale_y_continuous(expand = c(0, 0), limits = c(0, 125)) + 
  ggtitle("2025")
  
#My method seems to have slightly underestimated wild fish abundance
#need to look at where things went wrong
#likely somewhere in age assignment and particularly age assignment for outage expansion fish


final_total_plot <- ggplot(check_final, aes(x = spreadsheet_count, y = total, group = origin)) + 
  geom_abline(slope = 1, linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(size = 4, shape = 21, aes(fill = origin), color = "black") + 
  plot_theme + 
  xlab("Excel method") + 
  ylab("R method") + 
  scale_x_continuous(expand = c(0, 0), limits = c(0, 2000)) + 
  scale_y_continuous(expand = c(0, 0), limits = c(0, 2000)) + 
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Dark2", name = "Origin", labels = c("Hatchery", "Hatchery unassigned", "Wild")) + 
  ggtitle("2025")


summary_table <- check_final %>%
  group_by(origin) %>%
  summarise('R method' = round(sum(total, na.rm = T)), 'Excel method' = round(sum(spreadsheet_count, na.rm = T))) %>%
  mutate(year = "2025")
  

hist_by_origin <- ggplot(check_final, aes(x = diff, group = origin)) + 
  geom_histogram(aes(fill = origin), color = "black", binwidth = 5)  + 
  plot_theme + 
  xlab("Difference between estimates") + 
  ylab("Count") + 
  scale_x_continuous(expand = c(0, 0), limits = c(-50, 150)) + 
  scale_y_continuous(expand = c(0, 0), limits = c(0, 100)) + 
  facet_wrap(~origin, labeller = as_labeller(c(
    hatchery = "Hatchery", 
    hatchery_unknown = "Hatchery unassigned", 
    wild = "Wild"
  ))) + 
  theme(strip.background = element_rect(fill = "grey70", color = "black"), 
        strip.text = element_text(size = 12), 
        panel.spacing = unit(10, "mm"), 
        legend.position = "none") + 
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linewidth = 1, linetype = "dashed") + 
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Dark2") + 
  ggtitle("2025")

```

final_total_plot_24 <- ggplot(check_final_2024, aes(x = spreadsheet_count, y = total, group = origin)) +

summary_table_24 <- check_final_2024 %>%
  group_by(origin) %>%
  summarise('R method' = round(sum(total, na.rm = T)), 'Excel method' = round(sum(spreadsheet_count, na.rm = T))) %>%
  mutate(year = "2024")
  

hist_by_origin_24 <- ggplot(check_final_2024, aes(x = diff, group = origin)) + 
  geom_histogram(aes(fill = origin), color = "black", binwidth = 5)  + 
  plot_theme + 
  xlab("Difference between estimates") + 
  ylab("Count") + 
  scale_x_continuous(expand = c(0, 0), limits = c(-50, 150)) + 
  scale_y_continuous(expand = c(0, 0), limits = c(0, 125)) +

  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Dark2") + 
  ggtitle("2024")

comparison_table <- rbind(summary_table_24, summary_table) %>%
  rename(Origin = origin) %>%
  mutate(Origin = as.factor(Origin)) %>%
  mutate(Origin = fct_recode(Origin, "Hatchery" = "hatchery", 
                    "Hatchery unassigned" = "hatchery_unknown", 
                    "Wild" = "wild"))

grp_yr <- rle(as.character(comparison_table$year))
index_yr <- setNames(grp_yr$lengths, grp_yr$values)
```


We developed an R-based tool to estimate abundance and stock composition of Snake River fall Chinook returning to Lower Granite Dam. The R-based tool uses the same methods as the current run reconstruction methodology, but implements run reconstruction using R rather than Excel. We compared abundance estimates by sex, age, origin, and release group from the R-based and original methods. The estimates produced using the R-based tool aligned well with the original estimates (Figures 1 - 2). Typically, discrepancies between the two methods were small (e.g., <5). Differences between the two methods were typically centered around zero, indicating the R-based method did not show consistent, directional bias when compared to the original method. However, the R-based method consistently underestimated the abundance of wild-origin fish in 2025, which was a result of differences in the age assignment methods applied to wild fish after accounting for trap outages in 2025 (Figure 3). Adjustments to the R-based tool are ongoing to improve agreement between the two methods. Additionally, the R tool does not currently account for fall Chinook that arrive at Lower Granite Dam before the trapping season begins on August 15, so estimates represent escapement from August 15 - November 15. 



```{r, echo = F}

comparison_table %>%
  select(-year) %>%
  kbl(caption = "Estimates of Snake River fall Chinook escapement to Lower Granite Dam by origin for 2024 and 2025 using the original (Excel-based) and new (R-based) method.") %>%
  kable_paper("striped") %>%
  pack_rows(index = index_yr)


```


```{r final-total, fig.height = 12, fig.width = 8, fig.cap = "Estimates of Snake River fall Chinook escapement to Lower Granite Dam by age, sex, release group, and origin. Estimates account for fallback and re-ascension and trap outage, including an expansion for the end of the run.", echo = F, warning = F}
ggarrange(final_total_plot_24, final_total_plot, align = "hv", ncol = 1, common.legend = TRUE)
```


```{r diff-hist, fig.width = 12, fig.height = 8, fig.cap = "The difference in the estimates of escapement by age, sex, and release group between the original and new method. Estimates account for fallback and re-ascension and trap outage periods.", echo=F, warning=FALSE}
ggarrange(raw_diff_hist_24, raw_diff_hist, align = "hv", ncol = 2)
```


```{r hist-by-origin, fig.width = 12, fig.height = 12, fig.cap = "The difference in the estimates of escapement by age, sex, origin, and release group between the original and new method. Estimates account for fallback and re-ascension and trap outage periods.", echo = F, warning = F}

ggarrange(hist_by_origin_24, hist_by_origin, align = "hv", ncol = 1)
```
